tools.name: nogpu_report
tools.description: Free report: send an LLM's past decisions, 160-10,000 rows with at least 2 labels, either as `rows` ([{"text": ..., "label": ...}]) or as `jsonl` (the same rows as JSONL text; a JSON array or a CSV with a header row also works), at most 20 MB. NoGPU trains a small CPU model on them and measures what

tools.name: nogpu_status
tools.description:
A job's status, and its report once ready (same fields as nogpu_report). Also shows download_url after
        payment: GET it with header X-Claim-Token. claim_token and report_url are secrets.

tools.name: nogpu_buy
tools.description: Read-only, never pays: for a certified (fit) report, returns the $99 offer to keep the model, the question to ask the user word for word, a card checkout link for the user, and the USDC (x402) payment details when the server offers them. If the job is not buyable, returns the reason.

tools.name: nogpu_delete
tools.description:
Delete an uploaded job's data now (otherwise deleted within 24h, or 24h after payment if you bought the
        model).

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "nogpu_report" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: nogpu_report · Private data: nogpu_report, nogpu_status · Public sink: nogpu_report · Destructive: nogpu_report, nogpu_delete.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: nogpu_report · Private data: nogpu_report, nogpu_status · Public sink: nogpu_report · Destructive: nogpu_report, nogpu_delete

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
